newsitem.title: MEXICO: INTERVIEW-GMexico to open smelter expansion in Nov.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-GMexico to open smelter expansion in Nov.

text.p: Mexico's largest mining company Grupo Mexico, known as GMexico, expects its expansion of its La Caridad copper smelter will come on line in November, a company finance director said Monday.

"The engineers are finishing the project and it will come on line next month," Carlos Oyanguren told Reuters in an interview. "Whatever happens it has to be finished by the end of the year." The $110 million expansion is to boost annual capacity at La Caridad to 300,000 tonnes from 180,000 tonnes.

Oyanguren, deputy finance director of Mexico's largest copper producer, said the company's La Caridad copper and precious metals refinery is now half-built in its first stage. "It is expected that building will be completed half-way through next year, around September," he said.
Plans are to start a second stage expansion of the refinery to 300,000 tonnes from the first stage's 180,000 tonnes once the intital project is off the ground.

"Once the first stage is complete, it will be expanded to 300,000 tonnes," he added, saying there was no fixed date for completing this expansion. Oyanguren said total investment in the reifnery is $120 million.
Oyanguren said GMexico is currently increasing output at two multi-metal mines in the northern state of Chihuahua by 30 to 40 percent at a cost of $30 million.

The mines, Santa Barbara and Santa Eulalia, produce gold, silver, copper, lead and zinc and silver, lead and zinc respectively. "I do not have the exact percentages (of the expansion) but they are in the region of 30 to 40 percent," he said. He gave no other details.

Final studies of GMexico's El Arco copper and gold deposit in Baja California are expected in one month, he said. "We are waiting for the engineers to receive that study. They believe it will be in their hands in a month and the future of El Arco depends on what it says," he said.

Oyanguren said if the company goes ahead and develops the field, investment could range bewteen $200 million to $1 billion, making it by far the biggest investment prospect in the pipeline for the company.
He said the investment costs varied depending on the scale of the project and because the mine is distant without roads, electricity or water. "This makes the project more expensive," he said.
"This has to be taken into account, as well as the deposit, the price of copper, the outlook and then looked at as a whole to see if El Arco is practicable," he said.

GMexico will end the year producing around 340,000 tonnes of copper content, around 10 percent more than last year, he said. "We are going to produce around 340,000 tonnes of copper content this year," he said. "It was 10 percent less last year," he added.

Oyanguren said the company's only current copper cathode production was from its solvent extraction-electrowinning (SX-EW) facilities in La Caridad, with an annual capacity of 100 percent refined copper of between 22,000 and 23,000 tonnes. "It is at full production," he said.

The finance director said GMexico planned to close down an old copper smelter at its Cananea plant, currently producing 50,000 tonnes of copper blister, once La Caridad smelter expansion was on line. He gave no specific closure date.
He said the copper and precious metals refinery at La Caridad would produce around 2,000 kg of gold per year, although he said he was unsure of possible refined silver output.

Oyanguren said GMexico planned to bid in the government's rail privatizations. The company is the only one with a firm bid for the Chihuahua-Pacific line. "We are also going to take part in the Mexico City-Laredo line," he said.
--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com
